description: Pinned tool manifest for the Vibe Coder container image (Issue #4061). Every version the image installs is recorded here; container/Containerfile only restates these values as build ARGs, and worker/deno/tests/container_manifest_test.ts fails the quality gate when the two disagree. `providers` is the catalogue of pinned coding-agent providers and `installedProviders` is the set a default image build actually installs, which the Containerfile restates as the AGENT_PROVIDERS default (Issue #4105). A `toolchains` entry carries exactly one of `versionArg` (the Containerfile installs it and restates the pin as ARGs) or `fragment` (container/install-toolchains.sh runs container/toolchains/<id>.sh, which reads the pin from here with jq — Issue #1594). A toolchain whose `versionCommand` has no `--version` flag names the arguments that make it report its version in `versionArgs` (Issues #2070–#2073). A toolchain declares the `commands` it puts on the PATH, or — for a library such as PyYAML, which ships no console script — the Python `modules` it makes importable (Issue #1628).

images.name: docker.io/library/ruby
images.notes: Digest-pinned official Ruby image, itself built on buildpack-deps:trixie, so it ships bash, GNU coreutils (timeout), git 2.47, curl, ca-certificates, ruby 3.4 and python3 3.13 — still no apt install step to rot (Issue #4090). The floors are load-bearing: git < 2.41 keeps a literal --end-of-options in argv (Issue #3714), Psych.safe_load_file (Issue #3661) needs Psych 4, i.e. ruby >= 3.1, and the semgrep virtualenv is built on this interpreter, whose requires-python is >= 3.10 (Issue #650). The base ships no ensurepip, which is why the semgrep toolchain pins pip as its own artefact.

images.name: docker.io/denoland/deno
images.notes: Scratch image containing only the deno binary; copied in via a build stage so no archive extractor is needed.

images.name: docker.io/floci/floci
images.notes: The multi-arch floci image (OCI index digest) whose /app/application Quarkus native binary the floci fragment copies out via a COPY --from=floci stage; nothing from the image's own runtime is used (Issue #3367).

providers.notes: Coding-agent provider layer (Issue #4067). container/providers/claude.sh reads these pins with jq and verifies the download before installing it; the base Containerfile only selects the fragments via the set-valued AGENT_PROVIDERS build argument (Issue #4105), so a second provider adds a fragment and an entry here. Raised from 2.1.223 to 2.1.261 by Issue #1362: the CLI resolves the `fable` alias from its own bundled table, 2.1.223 resolved it to claude-fable-5, and in-container the image IS the update mechanism (skipSoftwareUpdateFromEnv) so softwareMinVersions cannot pull a running container forward. 2.1.261 carries Fable 5.1 as the default fable model (2.1.257) plus its prompt-cache fixes (2.1.260), and cleared the 24h dependency quarantine; checksums verified against the pinned artefacts and the arm64 binary run to confirm it reports 2.1.261. Raised to 2.1.281 by Issue #2560: 2.1.280 added Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) as the default `opus` model, which every substantive phase now requests by alias; 2.1.281 was the newest release past the 24h quarantine (2.1.282 was 5 hours old), and both checksums match the release manifest.json and the bundle carries the `claude-opus-5-5` id. Raised to 2.1.293 by PR #3432 review (Issue #3400): #3400 set `MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS.haiku` to 1M on the premise that the `haiku` alias is served by Haiku 5.5, but 2.1.281's bundled table still had `haiku:"claude-haiku-4-5"` — no `claude-haiku-5-5` string anywhere in that binary — so a container on it kept serving the 200k Haiku 4.5 for a 1M-windowed alias, defeating the large-input escalation guard (Issue #2393). 2.1.292 still resolves `haiku:"claude-haiku-4-5"`; 2.1.293 is the first release whose bundled table carries `haiku:"claude-haiku-5-5"` (`strings` on the downloaded arm64 and amd64 binaries) and was 30.1h past publish (2.1.294 was 19.6h old, inside the 24h quarantine); both checksums match the release's own manifest.json and the installed arm64 binary reports 2.1.293. Raised to 2.1.306 on 2026-10-22 (owner: the container runs the newest version of each provider): the newest release past the 24h quarantine (2.1.307 and 2.1.308 were under 24h old). Both checksums match the release's manifest.json, and both binaries' bundled tables still resolve haiku/sonnet/opus to claude-haiku-5-5 / claude-sonnet-5-5 / claude-opus-5-5. Raised to 2.1.310 on 2026-10-25 (owner: every container tool up to date): the newest release past the 24h quarantine, published 2026-10-23 21:20 UTC (the stable channel then pointed at 2.1.308). Both checksums match the release's manifest.json and the downloaded binaries, and both bundled tables still resolve haiku/sonnet/opus/fable to claude-haiku-5-5 / claude-sonnet-5-5 / claude-opus-5-5 / claude-fable-5-1.

The second registered coding-agent provider (Issue #4106) — the first addition made purely through the seam. Checksums are of the static musl release archives codex-<target>-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz from tag rust-v<version>, which run on the glibc base image. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,codex"` is what puts both CLIs in one image. Raised from 0.147.0 to 0.163.0 on 2026-10-22 (owner: newest version of each provider): the newest non-prerelease rust-v tag, published 2026-10-15. Both checksums match the GitHub release's asset digests, and every flag codex_executor.ts passes (exec, resume, --json, --skip-git-repo-check, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, --sandbox, -c, --model) is still in `codex exec --help`. Since 0.163.0 the CLI also spawns /usr/local/bin/codex-code-mode-host, without which every session runs with no tools (Issue #4323); codeModeHost.sha256 pins the separate release asset codex-code-mode-host-<target>-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz from the same tag, matching the GitHub release's asset digests, and codex.sh verifies and installs it next to the CLI. hostSha256 (CLI and code-mode host) pins the macOS archives <name>-<arch>-apple-darwin.tar.gz from the same tag, which the fleet PR babysitter installs on a host whose own codex is missing or older than its floor; a Linux host uses the musl sha256 pins. Bump them with the version. Raised to 0.164.0 on 2026-10-25 (owner: every container tool up to date): the newest non-prerelease rust-v tag, published 2026-10-23T04:48Z and past the 24h quarantine (0.165.0 is still an alpha). All four checksums (CLI and code-mode host, both architectures) match the GitHub release's asset digests and the downloaded archives, and every flag codex_executor.ts passes (now including --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust) is still in the 0.164.0 `codex exec --help`; `exec resume` takes all of them except --sandbox, which 0.163.0's `exec resume` rejected too.

The third registered coding-agent provider (Issue #4107) — Quorum's judge rather than a planner. The checksum is of the published package @google/gemini-cli-<version>.tgz, which declares no dependencies and ships the whole CLI as a JavaScript bundle: one artefact for every architecture, hence a single noarch checksum. That bundle runs on Node, which is why the Node toolchain layer is built before the provider layer. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,codex,gemini"` is what puts all three CLIs in one image. Raised from 0.55.1 to 0.65.0 on 2026-10-22 (owner: newest version of each provider): npm's `latest` tag, published 2026-10-20. The tarball's sha512 matches the registry's integrity field, and it still declares no dependencies.

The fourth registered coding-agent provider (Issue #415, parent #396). DeepSeek serves an Anthropic-compatible API, so it is carried on the *same upstream artefact* as the claude entry — this duplication is deliberate and must not be collapsed into the claude pin. Two things depend on it: the CLI is installed as `deepseek`, because both fragments run in an AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,deepseek" image and a shared binary name would mean one provider silently overwriting the other; and the version is pinned independently, because DeepSeek's endpoint is a third party tracking Anthropic's API surface and holding `deepseek` on a known-good CLI version while `claude` moves ahead is the point of the second pin. Pinned but not in installedProviders: a default image stays Claude-only, and `--build-arg AGENT_PROVIDERS="claude,deepseek"` is what puts both CLIs in one image. Raised from 2.1.223 to 2.1.306 on 2026-10-22, on the owner's instruction that every provider runs its newest version; the pin stays separate from `claude` so it can be held back again if DeepSeek's endpoint lags the newer CLI. Raised to 2.1.310 on 2026-10-25 alongside `claude` (owner: every container tool up to date); same artefact, same verified checksums.

toolchains.notes: Each of these repos commits its own shellcheck gate (quality/shellcheck.sh or an inline loop) and hard-fails without the binary — previously satisfied by a Homebrew install on the host.
private-repo-22's quality.sh lints its workflows with actionlint. Remove this toolchain if that repo leaves the fleet.

`cargo deny check` is not optional in these gates: private-repo-16 exits non-zero when the binary is absent and private-repo-17 runs it unguarded. The linux release is a static musl build, so it runs on the glibc base image.

Backs the diff-scoped mutation check (Issue #3393): Rust target repos run `cargo mutants --in-diff`. Upstream publishes only an x86_64 Linux release asset, so amd64 is checksum-verified and arm64 builds the pinned version from source with `cargo install --locked` (installed in the same run as, and after, the rust toolchain).

Secret scanner both repositories enforce in CI (Issue #1596). Neither drives it from a quality.sh — GRQ-AutoTrader has none — so this is the one toolchain the local gate does not run; it is here because a fleet agent that cannot run the scanner locally meets its findings only after the PR is open. The amd64 checksum is deliberately the digest the gitleaks CLI fallback pins in both GRQ-AutoTrader's secret-scan workflow and this repository's own .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml: one artefact, one digest. Only the local half can be enforced, and it is — container_manifest_test.ts fails the gate when this pin and that workflow's GITLEAKS_VERSION/GITLEAKS_SHA256 drift apart. Both digests are the release's own gitleaks_<version>_linux_x64/arm64.tar.gz entries from gitleaks_<version>_checksums.txt. `gitleaks --version` prints "gitleaks version <version>", which is what the build-verification loop in container-build.yml matches on.

PowerShell 7 for this repository's .ps1 launchers (Issue #1596). With the interpreter in the image the local gate runs the run.ps1 launcher suites itself (Issue #1598, IN_GATE_SCRIPT_SUITES in worker/deno/lib/integration_test_manifest.ts), and .github/workflows/validate-scripts.yml still fails loud when pwsh is absent, for the setup.ps1 suites. Checksums are the release's powershell-<version>-linux-x64/arm64.tar.gz entries from its hashes.sha256. No apt step: the runtime libraries the .NET host needs (libicu76, libssl3t64, libstdc++6, libgssapi-krb5-2) are already in the digest-pinned base, verified by running the extracted binary on the image.

The BATS runner both repositories' quality.sh drives over tests/scripts (Issue #1595). Without it in the image each gate printed "bats not installed — skipping" and the suites ran only in CI, where both apt-install the runner — NEAT-AI-core PR 597 skipped all 394 tests locally and ran them in CI. bats-core publishes no release asset, so the pinned artefact is the tag's GitHub source tarball (archive/refs/tags/v<version>.tar.gz) and its bundled install.sh does the install; the tarball is pure shell, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures. Pinned to 1.14.0, the current release, rather than whichever version each CI's apt repository carries — a suite that disagrees with it pins down to CI's version instead.

The spelling checker NEAT-AI-core's gate skips with a warning and NEAT-AI-scorer's scripts/spell-check.sh preflight exits 1 without, so that gate fails outright in an image lacking it (Issue #1595). A pure-Python console script with no standalone binary, so it follows the semgrep pattern: the pinned py3-none-any wheel installed by the pinned pip into its own /opt/codespell virtualenv, off the PEP 668 externally-managed system interpreter. codespell 2.4.3 declares no required runtime dependencies (chardet and tomli are extras only), so --no-deps gives a fully pinned install with no unverified wheel from the index — unlike semgrep, which still resolves its own dependencies there. One noarch checksum covers both architectures.

The runtime markdownlint-cli2, Graft, Playwright and the Gemini CLI provider need; the worker itself is Deno. Graft is the one consumer that also needs the headers this layer leaves in /usr/local/include/node, which is where its own rebuild compiles against (Issue #2097). Node 24 is the current LTS line. Its Containerfile layer sits before the coding-agent provider layer because a provider fragment whose CLI is a JavaScript bundle needs it at install time (Issue #4107). It ships an npm of its own, but the `npm` toolchain below owns that command (Issue #475) — one pin per command, so the version the image carries is never whatever the Node tarball happened to bundle.

Pinned separately from Node (Issue #475): the Node tarball bundles npm 11 (11.17.0 in Node 24.19.0, 11.19.1 in 24.22.1), so every build logged a 'New major version of npm available' notice and the image tracked whatever npm the runtime tarball carried. Installed over the bundled copy from a checksum-verified tarball, like the other npm-sourced tools. npm 12 requires node ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0, which the pinned Node 24.22.1 satisfies — bump the two together. Pure JavaScript, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures.

Drives the check-markdownlint gate stage against .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc; without it the stage SKIPs and structural Markdown breakage reaches merge. Pure JavaScript, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures — the pin matches .github/workflows/markdown-lint.yml so the container and CI report identical findings. It has no version flag: every argument is a glob, and a bare `--version` lints whatever the working directory's .markdownlint-cli2.* names — 134 files in the worker's own checkout, failing the start-up self-check on the first lint finding (Issues #2070–#2073). `--no-globs` drops the configured globs and `--version` matches no file, so the probe prints the banner (`markdownlint-cli2 v0.24.0 (…)`), lints nothing and exits 0 wherever it runs.

Backs the pre-push gate's spelling stage (Issue #3689): when a repository tracks a cspell config (GRQ: docs/cspell.json) and its CI workflow runs cspell, the gate runs cspell over the changed files and fails closed if the binary is missing, so GRQ's CI Spelling workflow (streetsidesoftware/cspell-action) no longer fails on a PR the worker already pushed. Pure JavaScript and ESM, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures; cspell 10.4.0 declares engines node >=22.18.0, which the pinned Node 24.22.1 satisfies — check `engines` again when bumping either. Installed from a checksum-verified tarball with --ignore-scripts, like markdownlint-cli2; the sha256 was computed from the registry tarball and cross-checked against the registry's sha512 dist.integrity. `cspell --version` prints the bare version, so the manifest-derived start-up self-check needs no versionArgs.

A worker RUNTIME tool, not a repo gate tool (Issue #2097, parent #2060): Graft builds the tree-sitter code graph the repo-context injection reads, so no monitored repository's quality.sh calls it and it is deliberately absent from REQUIRED_REPO_TOOLCHAIN_COMMANDS. The checksum covers the @nanonets/graft tarball only, exactly as markdownlint-cli2's does; its dependencies resolve from the registry at build time. Pure JavaScript itself, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures — what differs per architecture is compiled in the image rather than downloaded, by a rebuild of the native modules with no usable linux prebuild (upstream trailhq/Graft#119). Which modules those are and why every part of that step is load-bearing is in docs/CONTAINER-IMAGE.md, "Graft — the one layer that compiles"; findGraftRebuildViolations enforces it. `graft --version` prints the bare version, so the manifest-derived start-up self-check needs no versionArgs.

Standalone rust-lang distribution installed into /usr/local, so no rustup and nothing to update at run time. The combined rust-<version> package carries only rustc/cargo/rust-std/rust-docs, so rustfmt and clippy are fetched as their own component packages — hence the rustfmt_/clippy_ checksum keys, one per architecture. 1.99 is the channel the fleet's crates are moving to: four pin 1.99.0 in rust-toolchain.toml and already refuse rustc 1.98 through rust-version (Issue #3258), the rest still pin 1.98.0 — see docs/CONTAINER.md for the cleartext list. There is no rustup in the image, so rust-toolchain.toml is not consulted here: every crate builds with this pin, which is the 1.99.1 point release of that channel (a rust-version of 1.99 accepts it; `cargo --version` reports 1.99.1). Bump the repos and this pin together, or a new stable's clippy lints break their -D warnings gates.

Backs the semgrep quality-gate stage (worker/deno/lib/semgrep_check.ts, Issue #559): without the binary that stage reported SKIPPED on every fleet run and agents met SAST findings only in CI (Issue #650). The version is not a free choice — it must equal SEMGREP_IMAGE_TAG in worker/deno/lib/pinned_actions.ts, the semgrep/semgrep image .github/workflows/semgrep.yml runs, so a local pass predicts a CI pass; container_manifest_test.ts fails the gate on drift. Semgrep's CLI is a Python application with no standalone binary release, so the pins are the manylinux wheels, one per architecture — each bundles its own ~260 MB semgrep-core. Both are fetched by pinned files.pythonhosted.org URL with curl and the shared CURL_RETRY policy, like every other artefact in the build (Issue #1016); the URL embeds the wheel's compatibility-tag string, so bump that string in the Containerfile with this version or the fetch 404s. The `pip` entry under `tools` is the installer that puts them there; Debian's python3 ships no ensurepip, so the installer is an artefact in its own right and is pinned like everything else. The wheel is installed into a /opt/semgrep virtualenv rather than the system interpreter, which PEP 668 marks externally managed. Only semgrep's own dependency wheels come from the index unverified, the same residual risk `playwright-core install --with-deps` carries for its apt set.

The first library toolchain: it puts no command on the PATH, so it declares the modules it makes importable instead of `commands` (Issue #1628). With bats-core in the image (Issue #1595) NEAT-AI-core's `bats tests/scripts` suite executes rather than skips, and 31 of its tests then failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml' — its workflow-assertion suites parse workflow YAML with an inline python3 script that imports PyYAML, which their CI runners carry and the image did not. Installed by the pinned pip with --target into the interpreter's own purelib directory, so `python3 -c "import yaml"` resolves it: a /opt/<tool> virtualenv, as codespell uses, would never satisfy that consumer, and --target leaves the PEP 668 externally-managed system environment untouched. PyYAML ships a C extension, so the wheel is per-architecture and its name carries the cp<major><minor> interpreter tag; the fragment derives that tag from the running python3 rather than restating it, so a base-image interpreter bump 404s the fetch instead of installing bytes this manifest never pinned. PyYAML declares no runtime dependencies, so --no-deps is a fully pinned install. Verified twice: the image build itself (container/toolchains/pyyaml.sh imports the module and compares the reported version with this pin, so a broken install fails the build) and the container-build workflow's module loop, which imports each declared module through the image's own python3 and counts what it verified against this manifest (Issue #1705).

The code-structure indexer trialled as a second repo-context candidate (Issue #2153, parent #2145). Unlike every other entry here this toolchain exists for the worker's own trial, not for a monitored repository's quality gate — nothing in the fleet's gates invokes it, so it is absent from REQUIRED_REPO_TOOLCHAIN_COMMANDS; `repos` names this repository because parseContainerManifest rejects an empty list, not because a gate here needs the binary. Both digests are the release's own codegraph-linux-x64/arm64.tar.gz entries from its SHA256SUMS, copied rather than computed from a download. The release is not a bare binary: each tarball extracts a codegraph-linux-<asset arch>/ bundle carrying bin/codegraph (a POSIX shell launcher), its own node runtime and lib/, so the fragment installs the whole bundle under /opt/codegraph and symlinks /usr/local/bin/codegraph at it — the launcher resolves symlinks to find its own bundle directory, which is what makes the symlink work. `codegraph --version` prints the bare version, so the manifest needs no versionArgs and the start-up self-check probes it unchanged. Two consequences of the shape: the bundle is about 62 MB downloaded and 280 MB unpacked per architecture, well above every other fragment here bar rust and semgrep; and naming this repository in `repos` makes bakedToolsForRepo treat `codegraph` as baked for it, so a gate-skip finding for that command here would be suppressed — a no-op today, because no gate invokes it.

The RTK CLI trialled by the worker itself (Issue #2381, parent #2328). Like codegraph — and unlike every other entry here — this toolchain exists for the worker's own trial, not for a monitored repository's quality gate: nothing in the fleet's gates invokes it, so it is absent from REQUIRED_REPO_TOOLCHAIN_COMMANDS; `repos` names this repository because parseContainerManifest rejects an empty list, not because a gate here needs the binary. Both digests are the v1.0.1 release's own checksums.txt entries for rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz and rtk-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz, copied rather than computed from a download; the stable release is pinned, never a daily pre-release, and never built with cargo install. Each tarball carries a bare rtk binary at its top level (since 1.0.0 beside LICENSE and LICENSE-ENGINE), so the fragment installs it straight to /usr/local/bin/rtk and aborts if that layout ever changes. Since 1.0.0 the default rtk-<target> binary links the BUSL-1.1 rtk-engine, whose Additional Use Grant covers running rtk in production; the Apache-2.0-only rtk-oss-<target> edition ships alongside if that ever matters. The 1.0 CLI keeps everything rtk_output.ts drives — `rtk hook claude`, `rtk gain --all --format json` with summary.total_saved, `rtk recall` and the `rtk <version>` banner — verified against the 1.0.1 binary. `rtk --version` prints "rtk <version>", so the manifest needs no versionArgs and the start-up self-check probes it unchanged. The image also sets RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED and RTK_SUPPRESS_HOOK_WARNING: RTK does not honour DO_NOT_TRACK, so telemetry needs its own switch, which the binary honours. The second asks for RTK's daily missing-hook warning to stay off stderr — noise where the hook reaches the agent CLI through an explicit --settings path rather than the CLI's own user settings file — v0.49.0 read no such variable (the warning was throttled by a stamp file under RTK's data dir); the 1.0.1 binary does reference RTK_SUPPRESS_HOOK_WARNING.

Floci, the MIT-licensed LocalStack drop-in on port 4566 that the worker's own runs use (Issue #3367, parent #3346). The sha256 pins are of /app/application inside each architecture's image under the pinned digest; the binary has no version flag, so the fragment installs a /usr/local/bin/floci wrapper that answers --version with "floci <version>" and execs the native binary otherwise. Not started by the entrypoint.

tools.name: pip
tools.notes: Build-time only (Issue #650): the installer that puts the pinned semgrep wheel into the /opt/semgrep virtualenv. Debian's python3 ships no ensurepip, so pip is downloaded as its own checksum-verified wheel and run straight from that file as a zipapp — nothing installs pip into the image, and the system interpreter stays PEP 668 externally managed. Pure Python, so one noarch checksum covers both architectures. Bump it with the semgrep toolchain, or on its own when a pip release fixes an installer bug.

tools.name: playwright-core
tools.notes: Installs headless Chromium into browsersPath at build time (Issues #4069, #274), so the worker captures PR evidence with no host browser and no download mid-run. The version is not a free choice: it is exactly what @playwright/mcp@<PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_VERSION> depends on, because Playwright resolves browsers as chromium-<revision> and each release pins its own revision — worker/deno/tests/container_manifest_test.ts fails the gate when this drifts from PLAYWRIGHT_INSTALLER_VERSION in worker/deno/setup/screenshot.ts. The noarch checksum is the npm tarball (pure JavaScript, one digest for both architectures). Playwright's `install chromium` also fetches chromium-headless-shell — the binary a default `chromium.launch()` with no executablePath uses — and ffmpeg, which is installed with every browser, even under `--no-shell`. chromium_amd64 / chromium_arm64 are Chrome for Testing 149.0.7827.3 (linux64) and Playwright chromium revision 1224 (linux-arm64); headless_shell_amd64 / headless_shell_arm64 are that same Chrome for Testing headless-shell build and Playwright revision 1224 on linux-arm64; ffmpeg_amd64 / ffmpeg_arm64 are Playwright ffmpeg revision 1011. The build downloads all of those zips, verifies each committed digest, extracts them and writes INSTALLATION_COMPLETE before running `playwright-core install --with-deps chromium`, so the installer re-fetches none of them and apt only installs the system-library set. Apt packages stay unpinned by design: Playwright's install-deps list is large and Debian security updates move the versions; pinning them would break the next point release and blow the Containerfile size cap. Residual risk: `--with-deps` trusts Debian's signed apt repos on the digest-pinned trixie base rather than a committed per-package SHA-256.
